reference_drawer.title: 📖 Consistency Reference Guide
reference_drawer.description: Essential rules for classifying a pair of linear equations:

items.rule: Write each equation as a₁x+b₁y+c₁=0 before comparing corresponding coefficients.
If the x-coefficient ratio does not equal the y-coefficient ratio, the lines intersect at exactly one point.
If the x-ratio and y-ratio match but do not equal the constant ratio, the lines are parallel and never meet.
If all three ratios are equal, the lines lie on top of each other (coincident lines).

concepts.title: Understanding consistency
concepts.summary: A pair of linear equations is consistent if it has at least one common solution, and inconsistent if it has no common solutions.
points: Consistent systems have intersecting or coincident lines.

concepts.title: Three solution cases
concepts.summary: Geometrically, two lines in a plane can intersect, be parallel, or coincide.

concepts.title: Coefficient-ratio test
concepts.summary: Compare the ratios of corresponding coefficients of a₁x+b₁y+c₁=0 and a₂x+b₂y+c₂=0.

worked_examples.title: Type 1: Testing Consistency (Standard Form)

steps.reason: Coefficients are the multipliers of x, y, and constant terms with their signs.
Simplify each division of corresponding coefficients.
Since the x and y coefficient ratios are unequal, we stop comparing.
